title: 秦中感秋寄远上人
title_en: Feeling Autumn in Qin, Sent to the Monk Yuan
author: 孟浩然

text_note.zh: 第五句底本作“黄金然桂尽”。“然”是“燃”的古字，通行本写作“燃”。
text_note.en: Line five in the source text writes the word for "burn" in its old form; common editions use the modern form. The meaning is the same.

glosses.zh: 一丘：一座小山丘，指隐居的地方。
glosses.en: yī qiū: a single hill, meaning a quiet place to live as a hermit.

glosses.zh: 卧：躺下，这里指隐居、过安静的日子。
glosses.en: wò: to lie down; here, to live a quiet life in the hills.

glosses.zh: 三径：院子里的三条小路。汉代的蒋诩隐居时，门前开了三条小路，后来“三径”就指隐士的家。
glosses.en: sān jìng: three little paths. When Jiang Xu of the Han dynasty lived as a hermit, he opened three paths by his gate. Later "three paths" came to mean a hermit's home.

glosses.zh: 苦无资：苦于没有钱。资，钱财。
glosses.en: kǔ wú zī: sadly having no money. Zī means money.

glosses.zh: 北土：北方，这里指长安一带。
glosses.en: běi tǔ: the north, here the area around the capital, Chang'an.

glosses.zh: 东林：东林寺，在庐山，东晋高僧慧远住过的寺。这里用来指远上人住的寺。
glosses.en: dōng lín: the Eastern Grove Temple on Mount Lu, where the great monk Huiyuan once lived. Here it stands for the temple of the monk Yuan.

glosses.zh: 我师：我的老师，指远上人。上人，对和尚的尊称。
glosses.en: wǒ shī: my teacher, meaning the monk Yuan. Shàng rén is a polite word for a Buddhist monk.

glosses.zh: 黄金燃桂尽：带来的钱像烧桂木一样用光了。古书里说，京城柴火贵得像桂木。意思是京城物价高。
glosses.en: huáng jīn rán guì jìn: the gold was used up as if burning cinnamon wood. An old book says firewood in the capital cost as much as cinnamon. It means living in the capital was very costly.

glosses.zh: 逐年衰：一年比一年衰退。
glosses.en: zhú nián shuāi: fading year by year.

glosses.zh: 但益悲：只是更加悲伤。但，只；益，更加。
glosses.en: dàn yì bēi: only sadder still. Dàn means only; yì means even more.

translation.zh: 我常常想找个小山丘去隐居，
translation.en: I have always longed to live on a quiet hill,
but sadly I have no money for a home with three paths.

translation.zh: 留在北方的京城，不是我的心愿，
translation.en: Staying here in the north was never my wish;

translation.zh: 我思念着东林寺里的老师。
translation.en: I think of my teacher at the Eastern Grove Temple.

translation.zh: 带来的钱在京城像烧桂木一样花光了，
translation.en: My gold burned away like cinnamon wood in the costly capital,

translation.zh: 雄心壮志也一年年消磨下去。
translation.en: and my high hopes fade a little more each year.
At evening the cool wind comes,

translation.zh: 听到蝉叫，只让我更加悲伤。
translation.en: and hearing the cicadas only makes me sadder.

background.zh: 这首诗是孟浩然在长安时写的。秦中就是长安一带。一般认为，他四十岁左右到长安考进士，没有考中，钱也花光了，又到了秋天，心情很低落，就写了这首诗寄给一位叫“远”的和尚朋友。这位远上人是谁，已经不清楚了。
background.en: Meng Haoran wrote this poem in Chang'an. Qin here means the area around Chang'an. He is usually thought to have gone there at about forty to sit the imperial exam, and he failed. His money was gone, autumn had come, and he felt very low. So he wrote this poem and sent it to a monk friend named Yuan. We no longer know who this monk was.

author_note.zh: 孟浩然（689—740），唐代山水田园诗人，和王维齐名，人称“王孟”。他大半生住在家乡襄阳，曾到长安求官，却没有成功，后来一直没有做官。这首诗正是他求官失败时的心声。
author_note.en: Meng Haoran (689–740) was a Tang poet of hills, rivers and farm life. He was as famous as Wang Wei, and the two were called "Wang and Meng". He spent most of his life in his home town of Xiangyang. He went to Chang'an hoping for a post but failed, and he never became an official. This poem speaks from that time of failure.

appreciation.zh: 这首诗像一封写给好朋友的诉苦信。开头说：我想隐居，可没钱；想留下做官，又不是我的心愿。进也不行，退也不行。接着他说钱花光了，志气也一年年没了，话说得很直白，也很心酸。最后两句不再说道理，只写傍晚的凉风和秋天的蝉声。凉风让人觉得冷，蝉声断断续续，就像他说不完的愁。他不说多悲伤，只说“更悲”，读的人自然就能体会。
appreciation.en: This poem is like a letter of troubles to a close friend. It begins: I want to live as a hermit, but I have no money. I could stay and seek a post, but that is not what I want. He cannot go forward or back. Then he says his money is gone and his spirit fades each year. He says it plainly, and it hurts to read. The last two lines stop explaining and simply show the evening wind and the autumn cicadas. The cool wind feels cold. The cicadas sing on and off, like his worries that never end. He does not tell us how sad he is, only that he is sadder still, and we feel it ourselves.
